Mobile and manufactured homes in Mission
The parks and communities

items.t: Strata — Cherry Lane, 32165 7th Ave: These are strata purchases — Form B, strata fees, registered bylaws — NOT pad tenancies, NOT mobile stock. Briskham Manor is also NOT Briskham Hill (7540 Briskham Street, 19 new townhomes, 2025/2026) — same street, different form, different strata.

Life lease: Life-lease apartments for independent seniors, owned and operated by the Cedar Valley Manor Life Lease Society (Mission Association for Seniors Housing). The operator states the model plainly: you pay an entrance fee, you do not own the unit or the building, you purchase an interest giving you the right to live there, and at termination you receive back the original entrance fee less a set percentage for operation costs. NOT a condo purchase, NOT a park.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Mission

items.t: Municipality: the City of Mission, a municipality in the Fraser Valley Regional District, on the north side of the Fraser River, bounded by the Fraser River to the south, the District of Maple Ridge to the west, and FVRD electoral areas to the north and east.
The City's Rural Mission Strategy covers the rural communities of the city — the same communities carried as rural sub-areas.

Main roads and transit: Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) runs east–west through the city and crosses the Fraser River to Abbotsford on the Mission Bridge (Highway 11); Dewdney Trunk Road runs along the north side toward Maple Ridge. Mission City Station, 33200 North Railway Ave, is the eastern terminus of the West Coast Express, with trains to Downtown Vancouver on weekday rush hours; BC Transit's Central Fraser Valley system serves Mission with local routes including Route 31 Mission to Abbotsford.

Services: Mission Leisure Centre, 7650 Grand Street; Mission Library, 33247 Second Avenue (Fraser Valley Regional Library); Mission Memorial Hospital, 7324 Hurd St; Mission Community Health Centre, 7298 Hurd Street; Mission Urgent and Primary Care Centre, 304-32555 London Ave (7 days, 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.), at the main retail node on London Avenue at the Highway 7 / Highway 11 junction.
SD75 runs a middle tier: elementary K–6, middle schools Grades 7–9 and Mission Senior Secondary Grades 10–12.

Flood / ALR: the Fraser River floodplain runs along the city's south edge, and low areas such as Hatzic Prairie — where Mission Mobile Home Park sits — are protected by the Dewdney Dyke system; City taxes also carry a diking levy on top of the municipal, school, regional district and BC Assessment levies. ALR land sits mainly on the city's rural edges, with status parcel-specific on ALC mapping.

blocks.text: Good to know about Mission

items.t: Mission's 55+ map is two geographies, not one: Almost all of the strata / life-lease / co-op stock sits within a few blocks on the 7th Avenue / Cedar Street bench (Cherry Lane, Luther Place, Cedar Valley Manor, St. Andrew's Place, plus the Briskham Street pocket west of downtown), while the only rural 55+ product is the manufactured-home parks on Lougheed Highway — a park buyer and a bench buyer are shopping different Mission entirely, with different tenure law.

One listing's "First Nations Lease" line changes the diligence, not just the label: If the park's head tenure is a First Nations lease, the lease's term, consent and registration position sit underneath every pad tenancy in the park; confirm the head tenure from park documents, not the listing, before offering.

The rural park option comes with dyke geography: Mission Mobile Home Park sits in Hatzic, behind the Dewdney Dyke system, and Mission taxes carry a diking levy — the trade for the park's price point is floodplain-adjacent land and car dependence, so confirm the parcel's flood status and the pad tenancy terms together.

faq.q: Is Mission a city or a district?
faq.a: It is the City of Mission — the municipality's own site, bylaws and Official Community Plan all use "City of Mission".

faq.q: How do I get to Vancouver from Mission?
faq.a: By road on Highway 7 west through Maple Ridge, or Highway 11 south to Highway 1; by transit, the West Coast Express leaves Mission City Station (33200 North Railway Ave) for Downtown Vancouver on weekday rush hours, and BC Transit Route 31 connects Mission to Abbotsford.

faq.q: Can I add a suite or extra units to a Mission house lot?
faq.a: The City's SSMUH page states that zones previously restricted to single family or duplex dwellings are subject to the provincial small-scale multi-unit housing legislation the City has adopted; what is allowed on a specific lot depends on its zone under Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020.

The city's south edge is Fraser River floodplain, and low areas such as Hatzic Prairie sit behind the Dewdney Dyke system; flood status is property-specific — check the address against City and FVRD floodplain mapping before buying.

faq.q: In a Mission park, do I own the land?
faq.a: No. You own the home (a chattel) and rent the pad — that is not land ownership. Your right to the site is the assigned pad tenancy under the MHPTA, subject to park-owner consent on RTB Form 10.

faq.q: Is the park inside the City of Mission or the regional district?
faq.a: It matters: it decides the tax-penalty regime (City flat 10% vs the rural 5% + 5%), the servicing bylaw and the zoning authority. Confirm jurisdiction for the exact parcel before offering.

faq.q: Are Cherry Lane, Cedar Valley Manor and St. Andrew's Place cheaper park alternatives?
faq.a: No — they are different tenures entirely, not parks: Cherry Lane is a strata townhouse purchase (Form B, registered 55+ bylaw regime); Cedar Valley Manor is a life lease (an occupancy interest — you do not own the unit); St. Andrew's Place is a housing co-op (you join and pay housing charges — you do not buy a unit). Compare the documents, not just the prices.
